On-Chain Operator. Module 13 · The income engine. Navy and cyan. This is the door, not the whole module. Education only.
You already have a balance sheet. Income is only the part of it you can explain after losses.

By the end of the module you will be able to do this: design an income portfolio, measure expected income after expected losses, and set a payout you can sustain. Not before. The lessons earn it one page at a time.

The lessons, in order, are 13.0 Mastery Starter, 13.1 Income sources ranked by durability, 13.2 Risk-adjusted yield: subtracting expected losses, 13.3 Building the income portfolio, 13.4 The payout policy: how much you can take out, 13.5 Scaling, compounding and the annual review. You do not skip ahead. Each page is the input to the next.
Lesson 13.0, Mastery Starter. Mastery Starter. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 13.1, Income sources ranked by durability. Rank income sources by how long and how reliably they're likely to pay, not by their headline rate. You will write that down when you get there.

Lesson 13.2, Risk-adjusted yield: subtracting expected losses. Convert every headline yield into an expected yield after the losses it statistically carries. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 13.3, Building the income portfolio. Assemble an income portfolio and calculate its blended risk-adjusted yield and expected income. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 13.4, The payout policy: how much you can take out. Set a payout you can sustain through bad years, and the rules that change it. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 13.5, Scaling, compounding and the annual review. Grow the engine safely and review it like a bank's annual report. You will write that down when you get there.
Next is Lesson 13.0, Mastery Starter. Bring nothing but the habit: one idea, one drawing, the word Example on any number. Education only, not financial advice.
